notes: The sole home of every golden shape count in the campaign. No plan document states one; every consumer reads this file.

This is the ONE Phase 0A capture (R-10), re-read on the 0A tip at the phase barrier. Every block below was measured on the tree recorded in captured_at_src_tree and on no other; the mid-phase reading a668b91 wrote at 66072ea and the capture a0db656 wrote at 7bcff73 are both superseded in place, and the last two notes list every value that moved with its cause. Re-reading is not re-capturing: no counter, residual, rung histogram, winner, score or golden count below moved at either refresh, so the baseline this phase is judged against is still the one a0db656 measured (R-10, D-97). What a barrier refresh exists for is the opposite failure -- a receipt that keeps claiming a tree it no longer describes, which is prose outrunning code inside the campaign's own baseline. Baselines and this receipt move only in receipt-only commits (R-32), and only the integration agent writes this file outside R-32's three carved-out keys (R-34).

golden, coupled_golden and coupled_golden_exact are NOT re-captured here. Both committed baselines compare clean at the 0A tip -- 'golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json' and the same against scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json each report 'snapshot identical' -- so the shape pinned at 66072ea is the tip's shape, and Phase 0's single re-capture belongs to the 0B phase boundary (R-10, R-17, D-97). R-07: each legacy scenario's prior is recorded beside its measurement in the counter's 'prior' field, and the residual is recorded rather than asserted equal. Divergence cause: none -- every prior reproduced exactly (evaluations 1324/1033/706, proposals 1306/1015/688, memo misses 1249/967/577, pair fights 2735/3127/1446, residual 87/28/34), so those three families leave the PRIOR class. syndra_mandate_3champ is new in 0A.3 and has no prior; its residual of 330 is roughly four times the largest legacy one, which is the compiled-to-receipt routing cost R-27 predicted the cc scenario would expose.

R-08 determinism probe: five isolated repeats per scenario, all four scenarios. Every counter family, the residual and the rung histogram are 'exact' with spread 0, so each may be equality gated and none is demoted to a ratchet. Wall time is a ratchet by rule, not by measurement (R-28).

R-28 allocation_probe: tracemalloc peak for one isolated candidate evaluation, with the scenario's PROBE_BUILDS build locked into every slot so the optimizer's exact regime scores exactly one option. Three captures of each scenario per capture session, through 'bench_coupled_optimizer.py --alloc --json'; the recorded value is the maximum observed, observed_spread_bytes is the max-minus-min of those three, and the gate margin is Phase 4 S4's 15%. Three consequences a reader must not have to derive. (a) These peaks are LOWER than the mid-phase reading on all four scenarios, so Phase 4 S4's 15% margin is now computed off a smaller number than it would have been at 66072ea -- a tighter absolute ceiling, deliberately, because the smaller number is the true one. (b) observed_spread_bytes is a WITHIN-SESSION max-minus-min on one machine state, and it is NOT a noise band, NOT a tolerance and NOT a gate -- the only allocation tolerance in the campaign is the 15% margin in this same block. Three measurements say so at this tip: the barrier session's three captures spread 63/0/63/63 where a0db656's spread 63/63/63/126, a spread of 0 on cassiopeia_5champ that plainly does not mean the peak is deterministic; the in-process fixed-work probe of the same tip read cassiopeia_5champ 63 bytes lower than the --alloc maximum recorded here, so probe route alone moves the figure; and an independent R-35 reading of this tip reported syndra_mandate_3champ at 233874 (+1.3% over this row), which the barrier session's three captures could not reproduce (230830 / 230767 / 230830). Every one of those readings sits far inside the 15% margin, which is the point: a reader comparing a fresh peak against observed_spread_bytes will manufacture an alarm the gate does not have. (c) A peak that moves is judged against the margin, never against this field.

tests: 5149 collected, 0 skipped, 0 xfailed, measured on the tip with 'pytest -q'. The pin is the tree's real collected count, so R-01 row 1's 'pinned count + declared new' is read against a number the tip reproduces rather than against a number plus a growing tail of commit bodies. It moved 5115 -> 5149 across the six commits after a0db656 -- five of which added node ids and declared them in their own bodies, 802875a being receipt-only: 66a7086 +8 (row 11's routing predicate and its three reds), 3527b8d +14 (the four closed vocabularies and their source assertions), c6c6093 +1 (the producer-row annotation test), db9e946 +7 (the plan gate's paragraph reach), e75961d +4 (the fixed-work allocation peak). Full provenance of the earlier figures, which this receipt must not lose to its own git history: 5007 was captured at c05467f, before 24a0297 added five golden-instrument tests later in the same slice, so HEAD before 0A.3 collects 5012; 0A.3 took it to 5035; slices 0A.4-0A.10 took it to 5115 with 57 node ids in three new suites (tests/test_plan_audit.py 37, tests/test_transition_rank.py 14, tests/test_deletion_frontier.py 6) and 23 more across the four existing suites those slices extended (test_capabilities, test_data_registry, test_participant_timeline, test_survival_kernel).

pylint holds one row per src/ or scripts/ file Phase 0A touched -- the 19 files 'git diff --name-only 584071e..HEAD -- src/*.py scripts/*.py' names on the tree in captured_at_src_tree -- each scored by pylint's own json2 scorer through scripts/pylint_ratchet.py --scores. The row set is that command's output and is re-read at every refresh of this receipt, because a touched file with no row is a file R-01 row 7's ratchet does not guard: ability_spec.py was exactly that gap, touched by 3527b8d and unfloored until this refresh, and the barrier is where such a gap is closed rather than carried. The eight rows 0A.4-0A.10 added are scripts/plan_audit.py, capabilities.py, data_registry.py and the five survival/ modules; the nineteenth, added at this refresh, is src/calculator/ability_spec.py at 9.850746268656717 -- the score 3527b8d's body measured and could not write, because this file is the integration agent's (R-32). Every row here is an enforceable floor, not bookkeeping: 'pylint_ratchet.py --check' fails on any file scoring below its row (R-03). Five rows sit at a perfect 10.0 (scripts/plan_audit.py, scripts/pylint_ratchet.py, capabilities.py, survival/__init__.py, work_counters.py), so any lint regression at all in those files is a red gate. Three floors have been RAISED rather than merely held, each a deliberate tightening: item_support_effects.py 9.838709677419354 -> 9.839142091152816 and participant_timeline.py 9.698275862068966 -> 9.698795180722891 at a0db656, and scripts/bench_coupled_optimizer.py 9.950495049504951 -> 9.959514170040485 at this refresh, where e75961d's extraction of _run_fixed_work removed the branch count main had exceeded. A later commit landing any of those three files back at its old score now fails a check that was green before.

demonstrated_red is empty by construction rather than by omission (R-05): every gate 0A added ships a permanent negative test. Row 2/3 provenance exclusion by tests/test_golden_snapshot.py::TestProvenanceExclusion and the coupled producer sensitivity by TestCoupledCoverage; row 7's ratchet by tests/test_pylint_ratchet.py::TestCheckRatchet; row 8's void rule by tests/test_bench_coupled_optimizer.py::TestVoidRule::test_a_truncated_response_voids_the_run and its counted-pair-fight invariant by tests/test_work_counters.py::TestRungLadder::test_every_pair_fight_goes_through_the_counted_wrapper; row 9 by tests/test_e9_corpus.py's four failing-check tests (stale pin, empty selection, short selection, receipt-count disagreement); row 10 by tests/test_survival_kernel.py::test_every_fixture_item_name_resolves and ::test_the_rung_pin_rejects_a_mis_declared_rung; row 11 by tests/test_bench_coupled_optimizer.py::TestRoutingComparison::test_a_differing_score_is_reported, ::test_a_differing_winner_is_reported and ::test_a_routing_that_changes_the_answer_turns_the_gate_red; and row 1's plan gate by the nine failing-input tests in tests/test_plan_audit.py. Row 11's entry is honest about its date: when this file was written at a0db656 the row had no negative test and no demonstrated_red -- its check existed only as prose, so nothing could have driven it red -- and the R-35 verifier found that. The predicate ('routing_divergences') and the three tests above landed at 66a7086, before row 11's next cited green.
